questions.prompt: An open-open pipe has length \(0.85\,\mathrm{m}\). Use \(v=340\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) to find its fundamental frequency.
An open-closed pipe has length \(0.85\,\mathrm{m}\). Use \(v=340\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) to find its fundamental frequency.
At an open end of an ideal pipe, is the pressure variation a node or an antinode?
questions.answer: At an ideal open end, the pressure variation is approximately a node because the pressure stays close to atmospheric pressure.

questions.prompt: At a closed end of an ideal pipe, is the air-particle displacement a node or an antinode?
questions.answer: At an ideal closed end, the air-particle displacement is a node because the boundary prevents longitudinal motion through the wall.

questions.prompt: Find the first three frequencies of an open-open pipe of length \(1.0\,\mathrm{m}\), using \(v=340\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).
questions.answer:
For an open-open pipe,
\[
f_n=\frac{nv}{2L}
\]
With \(L=1.0\,\mathrm{m}\),
\[
f_1=170\,\mathrm{Hz},\quad f_2=340\,\mathrm{Hz},\quad f_3=510\,\mathrm{Hz}
\]

questions.prompt: Find the first three allowed frequencies of an open-closed pipe of length \(1.0\,\mathrm{m}\), using \(v=340\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).
questions.answer:
For an open-closed pipe,
\[
f_n=\frac{(2n-1)v}{4L}
\]
With \(L=1.0\,\mathrm{m}\),
\[
f_1=85\,\mathrm{Hz},\quad f_2=255\,\mathrm{Hz},\quad f_3=425\,\mathrm{Hz}
\]

questions.prompt: An open-open pipe has fundamental frequency \(220\,\mathrm{Hz}\). Find the frequency of its fourth harmonic.
questions.answer:
For an open-open pipe, all integer harmonics occur:
\[
f_4=4f_1=4(220)=880\,\mathrm{Hz}
\]

questions.prompt: An open-closed pipe has fundamental frequency \(120\,\mathrm{Hz}\). Which of \(240\,\mathrm{Hz}\), \(360\,\mathrm{Hz}\), and \(600\,\mathrm{Hz}\) are allowed ideal resonances?
questions.answer:
An ideal open-closed pipe has only odd harmonics:
\[
f_1,3f_1,5f_1,\ldots
\]
With \(f_1=120\,\mathrm{Hz}\), allowed examples are
\[
360\,\mathrm{Hz}=3f_1,\qquad 600\,\mathrm{Hz}=5f_1
\]
\(240\,\mathrm{Hz}=2f_1\) is not allowed in the ideal model.

questions.prompt: An open-open pipe resonates at \(300\,\mathrm{Hz}\) in its fundamental. Find its length using \(v=340\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).
An open-closed pipe resonates at \(250\,\mathrm{Hz}\) in its fundamental. Find its length using \(v=340\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).
An open-open pipe has length \(0.60\,\mathrm{m}\). Find the wavelength and frequency of the \(n=3\) mode using \(v=340\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).
questions.answer:
For open-open modes,
\[
\lambda_n=\frac{2L}{n}
\]
For \(n=3\),
\[
\lambda_3=\frac{2(0.60)}{3}=0.40\,\mathrm{m}
\]
\[
f_3=\frac{v}{\lambda_3}=\frac{340}{0.40}=850\,\mathrm{Hz}
\]

questions.prompt: An open-closed pipe has length \(0.60\,\mathrm{m}\). Find the wavelength and frequency of its third allowed mode \((n=3)\), using \(v=340\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).
questions.answer:
For open-closed modes,
\[
\lambda_n=\frac{4L}{2n-1}
\]
For \(n=3\),
\[
\lambda_3=\frac{4(0.60)}{5}=0.48\,\mathrm{m}
\]
\[
f_3=\frac{340}{0.48}=708\,\mathrm{Hz}
\]

questions.prompt: A pipe has resonances at \(170\,\mathrm{Hz}\), \(340\,\mathrm{Hz}\), and \(510\,\mathrm{Hz}\). Decide whether this pattern better matches open-open or open-closed behavior.
questions.answer: The pattern is \(170,2(170),3(170)\). It includes consecutive integer harmonics, so it better matches an open-open pipe.

questions.prompt: A pipe has resonances at \(90\,\mathrm{Hz}\), \(270\,\mathrm{Hz}\), and \(450\,\mathrm{Hz}\). Decide whether this pattern better matches open-open or open-closed behavior.
questions.answer: The pattern is \(90,3(90),5(90)\). It contains odd harmonics only, so it better matches an open-closed pipe.

questions.prompt: Derive the open-open allowed frequencies from the condition that \(n\) half-wavelengths fit into length \(L\).
questions.answer:
For open-open ends, both ends are pressure nodes. The length contains \(n\) half-wavelengths:
\[
L=n\frac{\lambda_n}{2}
\]
so
\[
\lambda_n=\frac{2L}{n}
\]
Using \(v=f_n\lambda_n\),
\[
f_n=\frac{v}{\lambda_n}=\frac{nv}{2L}
\]

questions.prompt: Derive the open-closed allowed frequencies from the condition that an odd number of quarter-wavelengths fits into length \(L\).
questions.answer:
For open-closed ends, the allowed pattern contains an odd number of quarter-wavelengths:
\[
L=(2n-1)\frac{\lambda_n}{4}
\]
so
\[
\lambda_n=\frac{4L}{2n-1}
\]
Using \(v=f_n\lambda_n\),
\[
f_n=\frac{(2n-1)v}{4L}
\]

questions.prompt: A pipe of unknown end condition has consecutive resonances at \(510\,\mathrm{Hz}\) and \(680\,\mathrm{Hz}\). Use the spacing to find the fundamental spacing and give one possible pipe type and length for \(v=340\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).
questions.answer:
The spacing is
\[
\Delta f=680-510=170\,\mathrm{Hz}
\]
An open-open pipe has adjacent resonances separated by \(f_1\), so one possible type is open-open with \(f_1=170\,\mathrm{Hz}\). Its length is
\[
L=\frac{v}{2f_1}=\frac{340}{2(170)}=1.0\,\mathrm{m}
\]
An open-closed pipe can also have adjacent allowed odd harmonics separated by \(2f_1\); then \(f_1=85\,\mathrm{Hz}\) and \(L=1.0\,\mathrm{m}\). The two given resonances alone do not uniquely determine the end condition.

questions.prompt: An open-open pipe and an open-closed pipe have the same length \(L\). Compare their fundamental frequencies and explain the geometry of the difference.
questions.answer:
For the same length,
\[
f_{\mathrm{open-open}}=\frac{v}{2L}
\]
and
\[
f_{\mathrm{open-closed}}=\frac{v}{4L}
\]
Thus
\[
f_{\mathrm{open-open}}=2f_{\mathrm{open-closed}}
\]
The open-open fundamental fits half a wavelength in the pipe, while the open-closed fundamental fits only a quarter-wavelength.

questions.prompt: An ideal pipe has one end definitely open. Its allowed frequencies are \(f,3f,5f,\ldots\). Prove that the other end must behave as closed in the simple air-column model.
questions.answer: One end is open, so it is a pressure node. If the other end were also open, the pipe would support all integer harmonics \(f,2f,3f,\ldots\). The observed sequence \(f,3f,5f,\ldots\) excludes even harmonics, which is the ideal open-closed pattern. Therefore the other end must impose the opposite boundary type: a pressure antinode, equivalent to a closed end.

questions.prompt: A pipe of length \(L\) has one end adjustable between effectively open and effectively closed. Explain how the fundamental wavelength changes between the two limits and derive the frequency ratio.
questions.answer:
With both ends open, the fundamental has
\[
L=\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{oo}}}{2}
\]
so
\[
\lambda_{\mathrm{oo}}=2L,\qquad f_{\mathrm{oo}}=\frac{v}{2L}
\]
With one end closed, the fundamental has
\[
L=\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{oc}}}{4}
\]
so
\[
\lambda_{\mathrm{oc}}=4L,\qquad f_{\mathrm{oc}}=\frac{v}{4L}
\]
The frequency ratio is
\[
\frac{f_{\mathrm{oo}}}{f_{\mathrm{oc}}}=2
\]
